record.paper_title: Initial state fluctuations and final state correlations: Status and open questions
record.original_question: What is the physical meaning of the event-plane correlations measured by the ATLAS collaboration, and can additional theory comparisons clarify their interpretation?

evidence.quote:
The meaning of the event-plane correlations
as measured by the ATLAS collaboration should be investigated further by more theory
comparisons.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions, the azimuthal distribution of produced particles in each event can be expanded in a Fourier series, and for each harmonic n ≥ 2 one defines an event-plane angle Ψ_n determined from the n-th harmonic of the single-particle azimuthal distribution (or, equivalently, from the n-th harmonic of the initial transverse energy/entropy density). For pairs and triples of harmonics (n, m, ...), one constructs event-plane correlators of the form ⟨cos(c_1 k_1 Ψ_{n_1} + c_2 k_2 Ψ_{n_2} + ...)⟩ (with integer coefficients satisfying c_1 k_1 + c_2 k_2 + ... = 0) that have been measured experimentally for Pb–Pb collisions across centrality classes.

Provide a quantitative theoretical interpretation of these multi-plane event-plane correlators. Specifically:

(a) Identify, for each measured correlator, the underlying mechanism in the initial-state geometry and/or the final-state hydrodynamic/transport response that determines its sign, magnitude, and centrality dependence.

(b) Determine to what extent the correlators are fixed by the initial-state cumulants (eccentricities ε_n and participant-plane angles Φ_n) of the energy-density distribution alone, and to what extent they are generated dynamically by the nonlinear mixing of harmonics during the medium evolution (i.e., separate the "linear" contribution Ψ_n ≈ Φ_n from the nonlinear-response contributions in which Ψ_n is sourced by lower harmonics).

(c) Carry out theory–experiment comparisons (e.g., event-by-event hydrodynamics, transport approaches such as AMPT, or analytic response formulas) that reproduce the measured centrality dependence of all measured event-plane correlators, including those involving Ψ_6, on a quantitative rather than merely qualitative level, and identify the physical content (initial-state property or transport coefficient) that is thereby constrained.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent theory work has clarified much of the interpretation: a nonlinear hydrodynamic response formalism reproduces lower-harmonic correlators quantitatively and higher ones qualitatively, while AMPT transport calculations reach quantitative agreement with the ATLAS data including higher harmonics. Quantitative agreement for correlators involving Ψ_6 in pure hydrodynamics, and the disentangling of initial-state vs final-state contributions, remain only partially settled.

status_evidence.title: Event-plane correlations and hydrodynamic simulations of heavy ion collisions
status_evidence.snippet: Hydrodynamic simulations qualitatively reproduce ATLAS event-plane correlations; quantitative agreement for higher harmonics (Ψ_6) is less good.
status_evidence.claim: Hydrodynamic theory reproduces ATLAS correlators qualitatively, with remaining quantitative gaps for higher harmonics.

status_evidence.title: Event-plane correlators (Phys. Rev. C 88, 024909)
status_evidence.snippet: Linear and quadratic response to initial cumulants reproduces lowest correlators quantitatively and explains centrality dependence as a mixture of linear and quadratic response.
status_evidence.claim: A nonlinear-response framework provides a partial quantitative interpretation of the ATLAS correlators.

status_evidence.title: A method for studying initial geometry fluctuations via event plane correlations
status_evidence.snippet: AMPT transport-model results are in excellent agreement with ATLAS event-plane correlation data, in contrast with earlier hydrodynamic calculations.
status_evidence.claim: AMPT transport calculations achieve quantitative agreement with ATLAS event-plane correlation measurements.
